facts.raw_span: a 2-month history of a painless mass on the right side of the frontal bone
the mass measured approximately 4.0 × 3.5 cm
was well circumscribed, soft, nonmobile, and non-tender
Laboratory studies and neurologic examination were unremarkable
a large, circumscribed radiolucent lesion in the right frontal bone without adjacent soft-tissue swelling
a lytic lesion of the frontal bone with a soap-bubble appearance, cortical destruction of the inner and outer tables, and an associated soft-tissue component
a lobulated frontal-bone mass measuring 3.7 × 3.3 × 2.8 cm
was hypointense on T1-weighted images, hyperintense on T2-weighted images, and showed avid enhancement on postcontrast sequences

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of a painless mass on the right side of the frontal bone, combined with radiographic findings of a circumscribed radiolucent lesion and a lytic lesion with a soap-bubble appearance, is consistent with an osteolytic osteoma.

The patient's radiographic findings of a lytic lesion with cortical destruction and an associated soft-tissue component, combined with the mass's soft and non-tender nature, are consistent with a brown tumor of bone.

The patient's presentation of a painless mass on the right side of the frontal bone, combined with radiographic findings of a circumscribed radiolucent lesion and a lobulated mass, is consistent with a giant cell tumor of bone.

The patient's radiographic findings of a lytic lesion with a soap-bubble appearance and an associated soft-tissue component, combined with the mass's soft and non-tender nature, are consistent with an aneurysmal bone cyst.

The patient's radiographic findings of a lobulated mass with avid enhancement on postcontrast sequences, combined with the mass's soft and non-tender nature, are consistent with a soft tissue sarcoma.
The patient's presentation of a painless mass on the right side of the frontal bone, combined with radiographic findings of a lobulated mass, is consistent with a dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans.
The patient's radiographic findings of a lytic lesion with cortical destruction, combined with the lack of significant laboratory or neurologic abnormalities, are consistent with osteomyelitis.

The patient's presentation of a painless mass on the right side of the frontal bone, combined with radiographic findings of a circumscribed radiolucent lesion, is consistent with an eosinophilic granuloma.
